I made a one-line fix, but I'm not sure it's the cause of the issue, and I didn't confirm that my new test fails without the fix.

**What I changed**
- **Fix:** In `getPairedItem` (`packages/workflow/src/workflow-data-proxy.ts`), `results.every(r => !r.ok)` is true for an empty array. When the walk back through the paired items finds no source to follow, the code then throws `results[0].error` on an empty array, which is a `TypeError`. That happens when an intermediate node has `source: []`, as pinned nodes do. I added `results.length > 0 &&`. The empty case now reaches the existing `createNoConnectionError` branch just below, so the user gets a proper `ExpressionError`.
- **Test:** I added a test in `test/workflow-data-proxy.test.ts`. It has `A → B(pinned, with a pairedItem) → C` in manual mode, and `$('A').item` is evaluated from C. It expects an `ExpressionError`.

**What I ran**
- `acdc-test test/workflow-data-proxy.test.ts`: 145 of 145 tests pass.
- `acdc-typecheck`: one error, in `src/expression.ts(218)` (`'bridge' does not exist in type 'EvaluatorConfig'`). I didn't touch that file.
- `acdc-lint`: it couldn't run because `tsgolint` isn't installed here.

## fix(core): Resolve $().item expressions in partial executions

In getPairedItem, an empty results array made `results.every(...)` true, so the code threw `results[0].error` on an empty array (a TypeError) when the ancestry walk had no usable source, e.g. a pinned intermediate node with `source: []`. Added a `results.length > 0` guard so the existing no-connection ExpressionError is thrown instead, plus a regression test. This is my best reading of the issue, not a confirmed root cause.
